name: Snow Queen Pothos
description: Snow Queen is the whitest of the common pothos cultivars - often confused with Marble Queen, but far more heavily variegated, with leaves that can be predominantly bright white with only flecks and brushstrokes of green. The effect is luminous and frosty, hence the name. It trails and climbs exactly like other pothos, but the extreme variegation makes it a little more demanding: with so little chlorophyll, Snow Queen grows slowly, needs consistently bright indirect light to sustain itself, and is more sensitive to overwatering and scorching than green or Marble Queen pothos. Give it plenty of bright, filtered light (without harsh direct sun) and let the soil dry between waterings, and it delivers some of the most dramatic white foliage you can grow on an easy-care trailing vine.
toxicity: Toxic to dogs, cats, horses. Symptoms: Oral Irritation, Drooling, Vomiting, Difficulty Swallowing
careInstructions: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil are dry - err on the drier side, as it drinks less than green pothos
Provide bright, indirect light to sustain the heavy white variegation
Avoid harsh direct sun, which easily scorches the mostly-white leaves
Prune regularly to keep growth full and encourage branching
Propagate from stem cuttings, ideally including some green leaf tissue so cuttings can photosynthesize
Wipe leaves gently to keep them clean and bright
Fertilize monthly during the growing season with a diluted balanced fertilizer
Expect slow growth - normal for such a heavily variegated plant
commonProblems: Brown, crispy patches on white leaves: Sunburn or low humidity - the white tissue is delicate
Reverting to greener leaves: Actually helps the plant - too-white sections can't photosynthesize
Fully white leaves that brown and die: No chlorophyll to sustain them - normal, remove as needed
Yellow leaves: Overwatering - allow more drying between waterings
Slow or stalled growth: Normal, or needs brighter light
Root rot: Overwatering or poor drainage

fertilizing.tip: Fertilize monthly during the growing season with a diluted balanced fertilizer
